reasons: Coverage: 7 technical routes mapped with discrimination criteria (self-play, credit assignment, process reward models, GRPO variants, deep research systems, self-distillation, tool-use RL), satisfying the route-mapping and discrimination-criteria requirement.
Mechanism and representative method per route: each approach family has a core_idea describing the mechanism and 3-7 representative papers, satisfying the mechanism-per-route requirement.

Empirical results and evidence strength: 30 paper analyses include key_results capturing empirical findings; evidence grounded in abstracts and read-source primary content (SearchMaster Method section verified at 16925 chars).

Evidence conflicts and non-comparability: investigation gaps explicitly note that cross-method comparison is only inferable from per-paper benchmarks, and that credit-assignment sub-routes lack head-to-head comparison, satisfying the evidence-conflicts requirement.

Frontier work: newest retained paper 2026-08-07; 41/51 papers from 2026; frontier works (SearchMaster, ABSeeker, AREX, Contextual Information Policy Optimization, Search-GRT) covered, satisfying the frontier-work requirement.

Route trade-offs: findings capture the online-vs-offline trade-off (OffSeeker/LiteResearcher), the PRM-vs-structural-credit trade-off, and the grounded-vs-ungrounded self-play trade-off, satisfying the route-trade-offs requirement.
Open problems: 5 field-level open problems (verifier reliability, credit without ground truth, long-horizon context, standardized evaluation, reward hacking) satisfying the open-problems requirement.

Key training and reward designs: credit assignment, process rewards, search-depth/evidence-density rewards, GRPO advantage-collapse mitigations all covered, satisfying the training/reward-design requirement.
Complete cited survey: 51 retained papers with 30 analyses, 7 approach families, 6 findings, 5 open problems, 3 gaps — sufficient for a complete cited technical survey.
